newsitem.title: ITALY: Karan makes menswear sexy, male and comfortable.
newsitem.headline: Karan makes menswear sexy, male and comfortable.

text.p: U.S. designer Donna Karan's autumn/winter menswear collection made its Milan debut on Wednesday with designs she said incorporate her definition of men -- "sexy, male and comfortable".

"Every principle I ever felt about menswear is what this collection is all about -- soft, stretch, comfort, tailoring, the body. I always see men as very sensual," she said after showing the ready-to-wear collection.

Karan crossed the boundary between jerseys and jackets, presenting what she called sweater-jackets, cardigan-jackets and sports jackets in stretch cashmere and corduroy. She created a tailored but unconstricted image accentuating the male body.
Jacket and coat collars were fastened high, some round like a cleric's or in a less austere oriental fashion. Others were cut as if the lapels were closed and buttoned to one side.

"Comfort is very important -- clothes that work in modernity, day to evening, clothes that are not where they've been but where they're going. That is breaking with what one thinks of as menswear but still holding the masculinity," she said.
She aimed to fill what she called a "tremendous void" in luxury sportswear.
"It is very important to look at a man's lifestyle...so that's how we approached the collection," she said.

Sportier styles included clean-cut bomber jackets neatly tailored at the waist in suede and leather as well as dashing all-in-one flying and jumpsuits. Colours ranged from sepia, slate and granite grey to plum, bark and rust.
"For evening I felt there should be endless opportunities of how men dress -- there shouldn't be one look. Women go out for black tie and have all these options but men hadn't," she said.

Evening jackets drew on exotic influences. Kimono-style black tuxedoes and ankle-brushing evening coats with Nehru collars were worn over white shirts and a black waistcoat which crossed abstractly over the chest in two wide bands.
U.S. designer Calvin Klein presented his second line cK Calvin Klein in a showroom, making it cK's first outing in Milan apart from a jeans display last year.
A 1,300 square metre (14,000 sqare feet) store will open in Milan in February and a London outlet is due to open in late spring to step cK Calvin Klein outlets in Europe.
One-button jackets with straight-legged trousers aimed for a lean, modern but relaxed look and colours were autumnal, ranging from charcoal, moss green and rusty brown through to aubergine.

Italian fashion house Moschino earlier cut a typically vivid figure, with outfits in scarlet, bright lemon yellow and vibrant blue and jerseys and pants stamped with lively patterns of question marks, reproductions of photos and its own name.
Black leather featured in trousers and jeans-style jackets, as well as in a pair of shiny leather briefs and a top made of just four leather straps buckled over the model's bare chest.
A simple, collared shirt sounded a patriotic note with one green and one red sleeve and a central white panel like the national flag, with "Made in Italy" printed across the back.
The shows move into their final day on Thursday when top Italian designer Giorgio Armani closes the five-day event with his collection.
